q: According to the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), what is the minimum permitted trade size of Schedule 40 rigid PVC conduit for residential branch-circuit installations involving multiple conductors?
n: Rigid PVC conduit smaller than 15 mm (½ in) trade size may not be used. Source: PEC 2017, Art. 3.52.20 (Size—Minimum).

q: What do you call the connection between the service drop and the meter?
n: The service entrance cable (conductors) runs from the service drop to the meter and service equipment. Source: PEC 2017, Art. 2.30 (Services).

q: Which kind of standpipe can only be used by firefighters?
n: Dry standpipes hold no water. Only firefighters can use them, by pumping water in through the fire department connection. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Standpipe Systems; NFPA 14.

q: In a building's automatic fire-monitoring system that uses smoke, heat, or multi-criteria detectors to sense abnormal conditions, which component is responsible for receiving the detector signals and initiating the alarm sequence?
n: The Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP) receives detector signals and starts the alarm sequence. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Ch. 10 (Fire Alarm Control Units).

q: What is FDAS?
n: FDAS stands for Fire Detection and Alarm System. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Fire Detection and Alarm System.

q: It is a visual or audible device used to warn occupants of an impending fire.
n: A fire alarm is the visual or audible device that warns occupants of fire. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Ch. 18 (Notification Appliances).

q: In designing a fire detection system for a residential kitchen, which device offers the most reliable performance by minimizing nuisance alarms from steam and cooking aerosols, while still ensuring timely activation in case of a slow-developing appliance fire?
n: Heat detectors do not respond to steam or cooking aerosols, which avoids nuisance alarms in kitchens, yet they still react to a developing appliance fire. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Sec. 17.6 and Annex (kitchen detector selection).

q: In a multi-unit residential condominium, which fire detection device is most commonly installed in bedrooms, corridors, and shared spaces to provide early warning of smoldering or flaming fires?
n: Smoke detectors are standard in bedrooms, corridors and shared spaces of residential buildings. They give early warning of smoldering or flaming fires. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Ch. 29; RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Residential Occupancies.

q: A type of smoke detector that has a small amount of radioactive material between two electrically charged plates. Current flows between the plates, and when smoke enters its chamber, this flow is disrupted and thus triggers the alarm. This type of detector is now being banned in some areas.
n: Ionization detectors hold a small radioactive source between charged plates. Smoke interrupts the current between them and trips the alarm. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Sec. 17.7 (Smoke-sensing detectors).

q: This type of smoke detector uses an LED that shoots a beam of light in a straight line across its chamber. When smoke enters the chamber, it deflects the light towards a sensor which then activates the alarm.
n: Photoelectric detectors shine a light beam across a chamber. Smoke scatters the light onto a sensor and sets off the alarm. Source: NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code), Sec. 17.7.

q: Which of the following is specifically designed to prevent the spread of fire through a building's duct system by automatically activating in response to high temperatures?
n: Fire dampers close automatically at high temperature (fusible link) to stop fire spreading through ducts. Source: NFPA 90A; UL 555.

q: It is intended to suppress the fire in a wide area.
n: A sprinkler system suppresses fire over a wide area. Extinguishers and blankets are for small, local fires. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems).

q: A sprinkler system that is used in high-hazard environments. All sprinkler heads are open, and when a fire is detected, water flows through all the sprinkler heads to flood the affected area. In this system, the pipes are empty when not active. Water is held back by a valve until the system is activated. It is designed to smother fires quickly.
n: A deluge system has open heads and dry pipes held by a valve. When it trips, water flows from every head at once, for high-hazard areas. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4 (Deluge Sprinkler System).

q: A sprinkler system that uses fine droplets to extinguish a fire. It is effective as the tiny droplets cool the flame, displace the oxygen which feeds the fire, and absorb the heat as they evaporate. This system uses less water compared with others.
n: Water mist systems spray fine droplets that cool the flame, displace oxygen and absorb heat as they evaporate, using far less water. Source: NFPA 750 (Water Mist Fire Protection Systems).

q: Which sprinkler system is recommended if water damage is of particular concern?
n: Of these, water mist uses the least water, so it suits areas where water damage is a concern. Source: NFPA 750.

q: In this sprinkler system, the pipes are filled with nitrogen or pressurized air instead of water. When a sprinkler detects a sudden increase in temperature, it activates and the air pressure in the system drops. This causes the valve to open and water floods into the pipe and the fire sprinkler system.
n: In a dry pipe system the pipes hold pressurized air or nitrogen. When a head opens, the pressure drops, the valve opens and water fills the pipes. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4 (Dry Pipe Sprinkler System).

q: In this sprinkler system, the pipes are filled with nitrogen or pressurized air instead of water. It utilizes heat or smoke detectors to send signals to a valve. Once the detector is activated, the valve opens to let water into the system; however, water is yet to be discharged. The sprinkler head must first detect an increased temperature indicating a fire before water pours out. This added safety feature makes this system suitable for museums, server rooms, libraries, data farms and other water-sensitive areas.
n: In a pre-action system, detectors must open the valve first. A sprinkler head must also fuse before water discharges. This double interlock suits museums, server rooms and libraries. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4 (Preaction Sprinkler System).

q: Which of the following contains nitrogen under pressure?
n: Dry pipe systems hold nitrogen or compressed air under pressure in place of water. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4.

q: Which type of fire suppression system, as mandated by NFPA 409, is best suited for airplane hangars, utilizing a dual-agent discharge method to rapidly mitigate high-risk fuel fires and prevent ignition spread?
n: NFPA 409 requires foam-water deluge systems in aircraft hangars, discharging water and foam to control fuel fires quickly. Source: NFPA 409 (Aircraft Hangars).

q: Which sprinkler system is best for electrical transformers or tanks containing flammable liquids?
n: Fixed water spray systems protect electrical transformers and flammable-liquid tanks. They control fire and cool exposures. Source: NFPA 15 (Water Spray Fixed Systems).

q: Which type of fire suppression system is suitable for residential buildings, allows immediate manual operation during fire emergencies, and is directly accessible to occupants without requiring activation by firefighting personnel?
n: Wet standpipes (Class II, with hose stations) are always charged. Occupants can use them right away without the fire department. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Standpipe Systems; NFPA 14.

q: The most common type of sprinkler system. It is usually found in office buildings, schools, high-rise buildings and other structures with ordinary hazards.
n: Wet pipe systems, with water always in the pipes, are the most common. They are used in offices, schools and high-rises with ordinary hazards. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4 (Wet Pipe Sprinkler System).

q: Which sprinkler system would you recommend if large quantities of water are needed quickly?
n: Deluge systems discharge large quantities of water quickly through all open heads at once. Source: NFPA 13 (Installation of Sprinkler Systems), Sec. 3.4.

q: Which of the following is not an AC brand?
n: Kohler is a plumbing-fixture brand, not an air-conditioner brand. Source: Manufacturer product lines.

q: Designed to be sat upon in order. to wash one's genitalia, perineum, inner buttock and anus.
n: A bidet is a fixture designed to be sat on for washing the genitals, perineum and anus. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (plumbing fixtures).

q: Which device is used to automatically transfer a power supply from its primary source to a backup power source when it senses a failure or outage in the primary source, and to return it once the power supply is normalized?
n: An automatic transfer switch (ATS) senses a failure of the primary supply, transfers the load to the standby source (such as a generator), and transfers it back once normal power returns. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 1, Art. 7.1 and 7.2 (Emergency and Legally Required Standby Systems – Transfer Equipment).

q: Which device is used to protect an electrical circuit from damage caused by overload or short circuit, interrupting the flow of current once a fault is detected?
n: A circuit breaker protects a circuit from overload or short circuit by automatically interrupting the current once it detects a fault. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 1, Art. 2.40 (Overcurrent Protection) and Art. 1.1 (Definitions – Circuit Breaker).

q: Which is used to protect electrical components against dirt, dust, rain, etc.?
n: A weatherproof enclosure houses electrical components so that dirt, dust and rain cannot reach them. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 1, Art. 3.12 (Cabinets, Cutout Boxes) and Art. 1.1 (Definitions – Weatherproof).

q: Which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
n: A generator converts mechanical energy (from an engine or turbine) into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Standby Power); PEC Part 1, Art. 4.45 (Generators).

q: A type of magnet found in generators.
n: Most generators make their magnetic field with electromagnets (field windings energized by an exciter). Permanent magnets appear only in small or specialized machines. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB) (generators); Chapman, Electric Machinery Fundamentals.

q: A device that seamlessly connects the generator to the electrical system. It ensures continuous power supply by switching between two power sources: the primary utility power and the backup generator.
n: An Automatic Transfer Switch connects the generator to the building system. It switches between utility power and the backup generator so supply continues. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 7.0 (Emergency Systems; transfer equipment); NFPA 110.

q: What is an ATS?
o: An automatic switch used in conveyor systems such as elevators
An electrical switch used in backup generators
An automatic switch that triggers the fire alarm system
An automatic switch used in a building automation system
n: An ATS is the electrical switch used with backup generators. It transfers the load from utility to generator power and back. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 7.0; NFPA 110.

q: It is where combustion takes place and is the heart of the genset. It supplies mechanical energy.
n: The engine is where combustion takes place. It supplies the mechanical energy and is the heart of the genset. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB) (engine-generator sets).

q: In a genset, it is where mechanical energy is converted to electrical energy. It has two parts, the Stator and the Rotor (armature). The stator is a stationary component that contains a set of electrical conductors that are coils that are wound together housing an iron core. The rotor is the moving component that produces a magnetic force that causes electrons to move and produce electricity.
n: The alternator (stator and rotor) converts the engine's mechanical energy into electrical energy. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB); Chapman, Electric Machinery Fundamentals.

q: The initial output of a generator is not very smooth and has undesired ripples or fluctuations. This part of a genset filters out these ripples to produce a smooth supply of electricity to meet commercial power needs. It helps eliminate equipment damage and safety issues caused by fluctuations, surges, spikes and overloads.
n: The voltage regulator smooths and stabilizes the alternator output, guarding equipment against fluctuations, surges and spikes. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB) (engine-generator sets).

q: In data centers, command ceriters, and technologically intensive office environments, a raised floor system is often specified as part of the architectural and MEP coordination strategy. What is the primary functional purpose of installing a raised floor system in such facilities?
o: Improve acoustic isolation by creating an air cavity that dampens low-frequency vibrations
Eliminate the need for an HVAC system by allowing passive air circulation
Provide accessible routing space for power, data, and floor boxes without cutting or embedding conduits in the structural slab
Increase the structural load capacity of the floor by distributing weight across modular panels
n: A raised access floor gives an accessible space for power, data and floor boxes, without cutting or embedding conduits in the slab. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB) (raised access floors); TIA-942 (Data Center Standard).

q: A collection of components displaying details and parameters, including current, voltage and frequency. It has switches and buttons for operation.
n: The control panel shows current, voltage and frequency and holds the switches and buttons for running the genset. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB) (engine-generator sets).

q: A residential installation is supplied by a standard single-phase system as per the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC). Based on this configuration, how many live wires does the system utilize?
o: No live wires unless a grounding g electrode is installed
n: Philippine residential 230 V single-phase service is commonly delivered as two live (hot) wires, each about 115 V to ground, with 230 V between them. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 2.20; MERALCO service standards.

q: A commercial installation is supplied by a standard three-phase system as defined in the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC). Based on this configuration, how many live wires does the system utilize?
n: A three-phase system has three live (phase) conductors. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 2.20; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB).

q: Based on standard industry practice in the Philippines and commonly accepted conventions under the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), what is the typical color combination for LINE / NEUTRAL / GROUND, in that order, for a single-phase system?
n: Under the PEC (NEC-based), the grounded (neutral) conductor is white or gray and the equipment ground is green or green-yellow. Line conductors are commonly black. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Arts. 2.0.6 and 2.50.119.

q: The standard service voltage and frequency provided by MERALCO for residential consumers.
n: MERALCO supplies residential customers at a nominal 230 V, 60 Hz. Source: ERC Philippine Distribution Code; MERALCO service standards.

q: Based on standard industry practice and applications commonly encountered in the Philippines, where are single-phase electrical systems most typically used?
o: High-capacity commercial buildings requiring balanced three-phase loads
Residential homes and small commercial establishments with light to moderate loads C D E
Large industrial plants operating heavy three-phase motors
Transmission and sub-transmission lines in utility distribution networks
n: Single-phase systems are mainly used in homes and small commercial establishments with light to moderate loads. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB); Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 2.20.

q: Which luminaire will you use for 8 m ceilings?
n: High-bay luminaires are designed for high mounting heights, about 6 m and above, as in warehouses and gyms. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Industrial Lighting); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.
